_doc: #628 Slice 2: this app's runtime rootfs is a real fleet LIBRARY APK, installed and updated by the Store exactly like cloud-lib-cal. Nothing here restates the artifact or the APK identity: `declared_in`+`at` point at the #618 artifact that gives the lib its content-address version, and `companion` points at the release.companions[] entry (build.json) that owns the applicationId and the asset names.
_doc_module: The ONE name. id = lib-{module}, label = cloud-lib-{module} (#474, the same rule regen.sh applies to every lib APK). Not written out twice.
_doc_kind: #628: was `artifact` (catalogue-only, see git history) — now `lib`. This is load-bearing: it puts the row in constellation-fleet.json's `apps` under the Libs group instead of `catalogue`, so the Store's normal install/update path can be handed it. `kind: artifact` made Fleet.parse structurally incapable of constructing an install/update for this row (`apps` is the only group it reads); `kind: lib` removes that ceiling on purpose — the whole point of #628 is that this 400 MB payload becomes an ordinary installable fleet member, no longer merely a catalogue description of one.
_doc_companion: Points at build.json::release.companions[] entry with this id — the ONE place the applicationId (com.diegonmarcos.cloudlib.rootfstermux) and the per-ABI asset names (Cloud-Lib-Rootfs-Termux.apk / Cloud-Lib-Rootfs-Termux-x86_64.apk) are declared. Not repeated here.
what: The glibc root filesystem this terminal enters through proot: claude, goose, hermes, agy, node, fish. Installed alongside this app as com.diegonmarcos.cloudlib.rootfstermux, sha256-gated against the digest carried in its own assets, extracted on first shell and never refetched while the digest matches — no network at runtime, ever.
